## Original definition (verbatim)

1. **FOS-000001 — Preserve precise context in existing diagnostics.** **S; no dependencies; §5.** Pipeline creation failure logs discard the available `VkResult` at [replay:1559](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay.cpp#L1559), with analogous compute/ray-tracing branches. Device setup similarly reduces failures to prose. Include phase, resource type/hash and raw numeric result; capture `errno`/`GetLastError()` immediately at OS failures. Fix compute/ray-tracing capture messages incorrectly naming graphics/compute in [dispatch:918](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/layer/dispatch.cpp#L918) and nearby ray-tracing paths. Start with these sites, then extend per subsystem. **Check:** inject distinct Vulkan results and verify distinguishable evidence. Do not classify every non-success as a driver crash or every capture rejection as unsupported pNext. This delivers immediate value before a common schema exists.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Unit tests with Vulkan/OS failure injection:** Distinct injected Vulkan results and OS errors retain their exact numeric values, phase and known resource identity after cleanup; an intervening OS call cannot overwrite the originating error.
   - **Captured-diagnostic assertions:** Compute and ray-tracing failures name the correct resource type. Controlled Vulkan errors and capture rejections do not claim a driver crash or unsupported feature without evidence; a successful control case emits no failure diagnostic.

Legacy identity: `FOS-000004`. Original source: [immutable historical definition](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/73f891d6c0cf498ac92e804d7d0f0cd344a083f5/local-docs/reviews/observability-sweep.md).

Shared requirements and grouping: https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/8. All original criteria below remain required. Source status statements below describe their historical revision; current delivery evidence is recorded separately. Original relative links are resolved below.

## Original definition (verbatim)

4. **FOS-000004 — Retain unrecoverable child loss in the controller.** **S–M; no dependencies; §2–§4.** [Linux shutdown:335](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_linux.hpp#L335) and [Windows shutdown:278](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_windows.hpp#L278) use the same boolean for “do not restart because done” and “cannot continue.” Their callers restart conditionally but otherwise continue to exit success ([Linux:1429](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_linux.hpp#L1429), [Windows:1035](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_windows.hpp#L1035)). Separate restart disposition from the retained worker outcome. Immediately return an aggregate unsuccessful result when assigned required work is unresolved. **Check:** E5/E6; clean worker; failed worker alongside a clean worker; failure before resource identity is known. Record the assigned range and unknown remainder. Do not fail all successfully recovered attempts just because a child once died.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Controller subprocess tests on Linux and Windows:** A worker lost before its first progress report produces an unsuccessful controller outcome, retaining its assigned range and unknown remainder. Repeat with another worker succeeding and with worker report order reversed; the unsuccessful aggregate is unchanged.
   - **Recovery control tests:** Clean completion succeeds; a failed attempt followed by verified completion of every required item can succeed. A skipped required culprit or unresolved range cannot succeed. Assert the controller result directly, independently of stderr and optional shared progress.

Legacy identity: `FOS-000005`. Original source: [immutable historical definition](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/73f891d6c0cf498ac92e804d7d0f0cd344a083f5/local-docs/reviews/observability-sweep.md).

Shared requirements and grouping: https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/8. All original criteria below remain required. Source status statements below describe their historical revision; current delivery evidence is recorded separately. Original relative links are resolved below.

## Original definition (verbatim)

5. **FOS-000005 — Separate replay-thread work completion from item success.** **M; depends on `FOS-000001` and `FOS-000004` for complete propagation; §2–§3.** [worker:1800](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay.cpp#L1800) discards the parse return and increments `completed_count` after processing; creation helpers return void. [normal replay:4553](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay.cpp#L4553) returns success after the queue finishes (E7). Introduce a thread-safe outcome accumulator independent of optional shared memory. First cover parse/read and Vulkan creation failures, then setup/validation/support/dependency exits. Propagate the result through normal replay, child and controller. **Check:** E7, missing entry, injected Vulkan failure, and mixed success/failure. Keep queue progress as queue progress. Unsupported required work must be unsuccessful under the declared policy, even when it is not a crash.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Replay unit and CLI integration tests:** E7, missing input entries, injected creation errors, unsupported required work, validation failures and dependency-blocked work produce the expected distinct outcomes and nonzero aggregate exits. A fully successful workload returns zero.
   - **Thread/mode matrix:** The same fixed mixed workload has the same final logical outcome in normal, child/controller and progress modes, with shared progress absent/present and one/multiple threads. Queue completion still reaches its expected count even when processing fails; it is never the success oracle.

<!-- fossilize-migration-v1:FOS-000005 -->

assumptions_and_risks: Planner inspected the detached base read-only and ran no build, probe or test. Current #14 and shared #8 were read through gh with explicit repository. Current #14 matches the immutable original. Submodules in the detached planner worktree were uninitialized; implementation/checker must populate matching required dependencies before builds.

A boolean-only failure latch would satisfy aggregate failure but cannot satisfy distinct-outcome assertions alone. Expose internal reason snapshots directly to tests; prose parsing is not the result oracle. Public richer result/API work remains out of scope.

Internal child IPC/status additions must be acknowledged as intentional protocol behavior; source-level preserved consumer fixtures do not establish mixed-version worker/controller interoperability. Test current paired components and existing unchanged messages.

Controlled child failure is different from worker disappearance. Existing #13 controller currently returns early for unresolved workers, so integration must not let a new controlled item failure discard successful sibling completion or accidentally make crash recovery permanent failure.

Shader/dependency parsing, module reuse and pipeline loop counters describe different work units. Define and assert queue completion per submitted phase; do not equate summed event counts or attempt counts with unique final logical items.

All commands require coordinator-published intent, unique receipt and verification_lock with a real child timeout <=600 seconds. The coordinator settles measured waits before the next budget gate. Do not nest locks. Use bounded build batches if needed; do not lower assertions or change timeout ceilings.

Four-hour bound, initial implementation plus three repairs and one replan remain unchanged. If a mandatory Linux prerequisite or gate is unavailable/incomplete, report it and route a decision; Windows execution is explicitly excluded by the user, not an unannounced downgrade.

cases.assertions: Concurrent mixed producer updates retain every expected reason and unsuccessful status with shared progress null and present; a clean accumulator succeeds. Deterministic barriers reorder successful/failing producers; bounded exact counters/reason snapshots do not lose updates. Distinct outcomes are asserted through results, not stderr.

Use a rejecting DatabaseInterface with separate size-read and payload-read failures, an absent required shader/dependency, invalid JSON, unsupported serialization version E7 {"version":999}, mismatched tag/hash and parse-with-no-acknowledgement. Assert appropriate read/missing vs parse outcomes and known identities; successful parse control has no failure. E7 never succeeds just because parse-only queue drained.

For graphics, compute and raytracing, inject at least VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_HOST_MEMORY and VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST through actual production creation calls; assert creation-failed outcome, exact raw value/tag/hash, nonzero aggregate, null outputs and cleanup. Add shader-module and initial-object creation rejection controls so these cannot disappear through callback true/parse success. Successful creation remains zero and preserves outputs/lifetimes.

For every pipeline kind assert compile-required then success fallback yields success; compile-required then failure and explicit skip retain unsuccessful required work; successful fallback is not a driver crash. Check loop_count>1 success and failure-then-success: prior unrecovered required iteration failure remains visible. Verify create/destroy counts and counters remain meaningful.

Deterministically unsupported shader and graphics/compute/raytracing pipeline create-info produce unsupported, not validation/driver-crash, outcome even when progress is absent. Selected unsupported work returns nonzero; valid support control succeeds. Test a support rejection in a main-thread initial object callback as well as worker setup.

Invalid SPIR-V with FOSSILIZE_REPLAYER_SPIRV_VAL ON and --spirv-val uses the real validator and records validation-failed; a valid minimal shader control succeeds. Trigger actual on_validation_error callback during shader/pipeline creation via a deterministic dispatch adapter; retain validation failure even when Vulkan returns VK_SUCCESS. Blocked downstream pipelines are dependency failures, not their own compiler crashes.

implementation.boundaries: cli/fossilize_replay.cpp and, if useful, a private cli/replay_outcome.hpp; no public library layout change.
implementation.change: Define an internal replay outcome accumulator with stable named reason categories and an unsuccessful query/snapshot. Use atomics or a bounded mutex-protected object; initialize all state explicitly, avoid shared-progress dependency and exception requirements, and keep memory bounded by the needed facts. Preserve known tag/hash and raw VkResult when available, with explicit unknown identity for run setup. Do not infer crashes from controlled errors.

implementation.boundaries: run_parse_work_item, enqueue_create_* callbacks, run_creation_work_item_setup*, run_creation_work_item*, enqueue_deferred_pipelines, on_validation_error and run_normal_process.
implementation.change: Audit all required-input and item producers: both database read phases and parser return/acknowledgement in run_parse_work_item; initial main-thread parse callbacks; device/setup exits; shader support/SPIR-V/validation callback paths; pipeline setup rejection, missing shader/library/base handles, and graphics/compute/raytracing creation helpers. Return meaningful per-item results or record a precise category at the producer. Avoid double-classifying a support/validation callback rejection as a generic parse error when its cause is known. A missing dependency is retained as the origin, and its unattempted consumers as dependency-blocked rather than additional driver failures.

Preserve successful compile-required fallback: intermediate VK_PIPELINE_COMPILE_REQUIRED followed by VK_SUCCESS can succeed; an unrecovered/explicitly skipped selected compile-required item is unsuccessful under the required-work policy. Preserve successful invocation flags, loop_count, pipeline output cleanup and positive counts. Any creation failure in required benchmark iterations cannot disappear behind a later loop success. Only actual successful work may be marked as replayed/validated; this is not a complete redesign of persistent replayer-cache trust. Keep intentional input range/whitelist exclusions separate from selected but unsupported required work.

implementation.boundaries: cli/fossilize_replay_linux.hpp, cli/fossilize_replay_windows.hpp, cli/replay_worker_outcome.hpp, progress wrapper and ExternalReplayer status observation. An additive internal terminal record or reserved internal status may be used if documented and tested; existing progress/resume message meanings stay unchanged. Do not extend public SharedControlBlock or ExternalReplayer layouts for this slice.
implementation.change: After joining/draining queues, return the retained normal-process outcome. Give orderly child completion with item failures an authoritative terminal path independent of optional shared memory and diagnostic-ring forwarding. The controller must retain that unsuccessful result, avoid treating it as a crash or endlessly retrying it, and allow other orderly children to finish so successful sibling order cannot erase failures. Retain #13 unresolved-loss/range/recovery rules. Use the same shared policy in Linux and Windows source.

Add explicit Release-active checks in registered replay outcome unit/private production-inclusion and real CLI integration fixtures, isolated work directories and watchdogs. Link test targets with the same exception and sanitizer settings and enable SPIR-V validation in relevant fixtures. Update existing #13 Release parser-rejection compatibility expectations from false success to intentional nonzero controlled failure, without weakening the Debug worker-loss checks. Update local-docs/verification.md with registration, scope and intentional behavior/protocol compatibility boundaries; add one short factual [Observability] CHANGELOG.md entry with the full issue link.

non_goals: Do not implement the entire proposed observability standard, a public structured-result API/schema, durable cache guarantees, full retry reconciliation, cancellation redesign, Steam scheduling, new public ABI, or unrelated persistence/capture fixes.
Do not introduce production fault-injection CLI switches or environment hooks. Private production-inclusion fixtures and deterministic Vulkan/database adapters belong to test translation units.

Do not claim physical-driver compilation, cache warming/reuse, runtime validation-layer compatibility, native Windows/Apple/Android execution or general C++ binary ABI compatibility from null-device Linux tests.

No harness source or helper behavior changes are planned. The separate change-harness Python component suite is outside this C++ slice; its mandatory full-discovery procedure applies when checking that component. Run the full applicable CPU CTest inventory here, including its existing harness-style C++ fixtures.
